title: SIMFONI AI model: rationale, access, privacy testing and safeguards
asked: Two MPs asked about the Singapore Medical Foundation AI Model (SIMFONI): its rationale and cost, clinician access including private practitioners, safeguards for patient identifiers, independent privacy testing before deployment, and publication of test standards and findings.
asked_by: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
response: Mr Ong Ye Kung said SIMFONI develops AI tools for clinical decision support in chronic conditions, prioritising high disease burden and feasibility. It starts in a couple of specialty areas and settings in public healthcare, with possible expansion to more specialities and private practitioners. Models are built on existing international models, adapted using local de-identified patient data on the TRUST platform established in 2022, and an independent safety and evaluation unit will test them before deployment. On supplementary questions, he said the approach is a careful use-case one, with deployment in accordance with clinical protocols and clinicians still making the judgement; on data, he said a balanced approach is needed, using data with anonymisation and de-identification, and that TRUST data has been used incident-free.

left_open: Rationale for targeting conditions diagnosable by routine tests rather than rare diseases
Whether private practitioners will be included
Specific safeguards to detect and mitigate automation bias
Whether privacy testing will check if models can memorise or reproduce identifiable patient information
Publication of test standards, findings and response protocol for any disclosure
Scope of data to be used for training, including whether it includes all health data and the National Electronic Health Record database
Whether explicit consent will be sought before patient data is used for training
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered automation bias in clinical AI and data privacy, consent, scope and leak assurances.
